title: Epic: Combine PromptShield and Bifrost into one production gateway product
description:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- The product is one gateway product from the customer point of view.
- Public model traffic enters through the product `/v1/*` endpoint and is screened by PromptShield before any provider routing happens.
- Bifrost is the downstream provider/router/governance engine behind PromptShield.
- PromptShield enforcement is inline before provider routing; blocked requests must not reach Bifrost or any model provider.
- Minimal production gateway scope: one deployable Docker Compose product, unified gateway path, PromptShield pre-routing checks, one dashboard surface, and clear production environment configuration.
- The product must preserve OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` behavior for clients.
- Provider secrets and routing configuration must belong to Bifrost, not duplicate PromptShield provider/key settings in the unified product UX.
- PromptShield policy and audit views remain first-class security features in the dashboard.

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Requests to the public `/v1/chat/completions` path flow through PromptShield before Bifrost.
- [ ] A PromptShield-blocked request produces no Bifrost/provider request.
- [ ] Bifrost remains reachable only as an internal downstream for inference traffic in production docs/config, except for explicitly marked local/admin access.
- [ ] Dashboard/product navigation presents one coherent product surface for gateway health, security policy, audit, and routing/provider management.
- [ ] PromptShield provider/key configuration is removed, hidden, or reframed so it cannot compete with Bifrost as the provider control plane.
- [ ] Production Compose/env docs identify required secrets, pinned image versions, health checks, and no-secret-in-repo guidance.
- [ ] Automated verification covers route topology, config parsing, dashboard API behavior, and at least one blocked-request path.
- [ ] All relevant tests and type checks pass.

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- FORBIDDEN: Publicly exposing Bifrost `/v1/*` in production, because it bypasses PromptShield enforcement.
- FORBIDDEN: Maintaining two competing provider/key stores in the product UX, because operators will configure the wrong layer.
- FORBIDDEN: Storing provider API keys in repo-tracked files or example data, because secrets can leak through git or forks.
- FORBIDDEN: Using `maximhq/bifrost:latest` for production acceptance, because unpinned gateway versions make deployments non-reproducible.
- FORBIDDEN: Replacing Bifrost routing with PromptShield model routing for this epic, because the chosen product architecture makes Bifrost the router.
- FORBIDDEN: Building a custom gateway/router from scratch, because current Compose already provides the correct runtime chain.
- FORBIDDEN: TODO/stub implementation for core request flow, health checks, or security enforcement.

## Approach
Use the existing runtime shape as the backbone: Nginx routes `/v1/*` to PromptShield Gateway, PromptShield Gateway performs policy enforcement and forwards allowed OpenAI-compatible requests to Bifrost at `http://bifrost:8081/v1`, and Bifrost performs provider selection, routing, keys, governance, and logs.

The main implementation work is product consolidation, not a rewrite. The dashboard should stop treating PromptShield provider configuration as the primary gateway setup. Instead, it should expose PromptShield policy/audit/engine controls and Bifrost routing/provider management as parts of one gateway product. For the minimal production version, Bifrost management can start as status plus an authenticated/admin link or read-only summary if full Bifrost API integration is too large; subsequent tasks can deepen integration through Bifrost `/api/*`.

Deployment work should harden the existing Compose setup: pin Bifrost image version, remove secret-bearing data from tracked files, clarify env variables, preserve health checks, and document that production inference traffic must not bypass PromptShield.

## Architecture
- Public entry: Nginx listens on 80/443 and routes `/v1/` to PromptShield Gateway.
- Security layer: PromptShield Gateway screens requests using `policy.yaml` and PromptShield Engine.
- Routing layer: Bifrost receives only allowed requests from PromptShield and handles provider/model/key routing.
- Product UI: PromptShield dashboard becomes the single admin surface for security, audit, health, config, and routing entry points.
- Data stores: PromptShield dashboard uses Postgres for auth/audit/policy metadata. Bifrost uses its `/app/data` volume for config and logs.
- Audit: PromptShield audit events are ingested by dashboard through the existing log forwarder or direct audit push.

## Design Rationale
### Problem
The repo already deploys PromptShield and Bifrost together, but the product boundary is not yet clean. Operators can see PromptShield gateway provider settings and Bifrost UI separately, which creates duplicate control planes and an unclear production story.

### Research Findings
Codebase:
- `docker-compose.yml` routes PromptShield Gateway upstream to `http://bifrost:8081/v1` using `PROMPTSHIELD_PROVIDER=openai-compatible`.
- `nginx/nginx.conf` sends public `/v1/` traffic to PromptShield and exposes Bifrost UI at `/bifrost/`.
- `README.md` already describes the intended runtime chain: PromptShield Gateway to Bifrost to LLM providers.
- `promptshield-src/packages/api/src/routers/gateway.ts` still manages PromptShield provider, model route, upstream, and API key env settings.
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.config.tsx` exposes PromptShield gateway/engine config but not Bifrost as the product router.
- `bifrost-data/config.db` contains provider/key/routing/governance tables; `logs.db` contains provider/model/token/cost/status logs.

External:
- Bifrost docs describe Docker persistence through `/app/data` containing `config.json`, `config.db`, and `logs.db`.
- Bifrost provider configuration is available through Web UI and `/api/providers`.
- Bifrost governance routing uses virtual keys for provider/model/key restrictions and weighted routing.
- Bifrost supports an OpenAI-compatible gateway API suitable as PromptShield's downstream.
Sources: https://docs.getbifrost.ai/quickstart/gateway/setting-up, https://docs.getbifrost.ai/quickstart/gateway/provider-configuration, https://docs.getbifrost.ai/features/governance/routing, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost

### Approaches Considered
#### 1. Bifrost as router, PromptShield as inline security layer - CHOSEN
What it is: Keep public `/v1/*` on PromptShield. PromptShield enforces policy before forwarding to Bifrost. Bifrost owns provider routing, keys, governance, and provider logs.

Pros:
- Matches current Compose and README.
- Lowest implementation risk.
- Clear product story: secure AI gateway with pre-routing protection.
- Uses each component for its strongest role.

Cons:
- Requires dashboard/product cleanup to avoid duplicate gateway/provider concepts.
- Full Bifrost API integration may require follow-up tasks.

Chosen because: It directly matches the user's decisions and the existing production topology.

#### 2. PromptShield owns routing, Bifrost hidden as backend - REJECTED
What it is: Continue configuring providers and model routes in PromptShield, with Bifrost as a generic upstream.

Pros:
- Less immediate dashboard change.

Cons:
- Duplicates Bifrost routing.
- Confuses operators with two places to configure providers.
- Undermines Bifrost's governance/routing value.

Rejected because: It conflicts with the one-gateway-product architecture where Bifrost is the router.
Do not revisit unless Bifrost is removed from the product.

#### 3. Replace PromptShield Gateway with Bifrost plugin/guardrail integration - REJECTED
What it is: Implement PromptShield checks inside Bifrost as a plugin or custom integration.

Pros:
- Could become one runtime process.

Cons:
- Much larger scope.
- Depends on Bifrost plugin internals and version compatibility.
- Riskier than the existing working proxy chain.

Rejected because: It is not minimal production gateway scope.
Do not revisit unless a later epic explicitly targets a single-process gateway architecture.

## Scope Boundaries
In scope:
- Clarify and harden the existing Compose/Nginx runtime chain.
- Make PromptShield pre-routing enforcement the required public request path.
- Reframe dashboard UX/API around one product and Bifrost as routing control plane.
- Production env/docs cleanup.
- Tests and verification for topology and blocked-request behavior.

Out of scope:
- Building a custom router.
- Replacing Bifrost internals.
- Multi-tenant enterprise RBAC/governance beyond what Bifrost already provides.
- Full custom Bifrost dashboard clone if an authenticated/admin link or API-backed minimal summary is sufficient for first production version.
- Response scanning as a required first-version feature; pre-routing enforcement is the chosen requirement.

## Open Questions
- Should `/bifrost/` remain exposed through Nginx for local/admin use, or be removed from production Nginx and accessed only through a private network/tunnel?
- Should first production dashboard integration call Bifrost `/api/providers` directly, or start with health/status plus an admin link?
- Which exact Bifrost image tag should be pinned for production?
- Should existing tracked `bifrost-data` be removed from git and replaced with sanitized bootstrap docs?

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)
### Key Decisions Made
| Question | User Answer | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| What should the combined product be from the customer point of view? | One gateway product | Dashboard/docs/deployment must tell one product story, not two separate tools. |
| Where should PromptShield enforcement happen? | Inline before provider routing | PromptShield must sit before Bifrost; blocked requests cannot reach Bifrost/providers. |
| What is the production success target? | Minimal production gateway | Avoid enterprise scope and large rewrites; harden the existing Compose product. |

### Research Deep-Dives
#### Runtime topology
Question explored: Does the repo already connect PromptShield and Bifrost in the desired order?
Sources consulted: `docker-compose.yml`, `nginx/nginx.conf`, `README.md`.
Findings: Compose and README already implement the desired chain. Nginx routes `/v1/` to PromptShield; PromptShield forwards to Bifrost using OpenAI-compatible upstream.
Conclusion: Preserve the topology and improve product boundaries.

#### Dashboard ownership model
Question explored: Which layer currently owns gateway/provider config in the dashboard?
Sources consulted: `gateway.ts`, `_layout.config.tsx`, `_layout.gateway.tsx`, `_layout.tsx`.
Findings: PromptShield dashboard has code for PromptShield provider/key/model settings, but the current nav exposes config rather than a Bifrost-first routing surface.
Conclusion: The unified product needs dashboard/API cleanup so Bifrost is the router and PromptShield is the security layer.

#### Bifrost capabilities
Question explored: Can Bifrost serve as provider/router control plane for this product?
Sources consulted: local `bifrost-data` SQLite schemas and Bifrost docs.
Findings: Bifrost provides provider config, keys, virtual keys, routing rules, logs, token/cost fields, and OpenAI-compatible inference.
Conclusion: Use Bifrost as downstream router and avoid duplicating those functions in PromptShield.

### Dead-End Paths
#### Custom combined gateway
Why explored: A single gateway binary could seem cleaner.
Investigation: Existing Compose already wires two working components; Bifrost plugin replacement would be larger and version-sensitive.
Why abandoned: Not needed for minimal production and increases risk.

#### PromptShield multi-provider routing as the main router
Why explored: PromptShield already has provider env and model route support.
Investigation: Bifrost is present specifically as an AI gateway/router with richer provider governance.
Why abandoned: Creates duplicate router ownership and contradicts the chosen one-gateway-product direction.

### Open Concerns Raised
- None beyond the three core architecture choices; remaining questions are implementation details for the first tasks.
close_reason: Combined PromptShield and Bifrost into a single production gateway product with PromptShield pre-routing enforcement, Bifrost provider control plane ownership, internal component ports, hardened admin defaults, and verifier coverage.

title: Task 1: Codify and verify the production gateway topology
description:
## Goal
Codify and verify the minimal production gateway topology before changing product UI: public inference must enter through PromptShield, PromptShield must forward allowed traffic to Bifrost, and production config/docs must not encourage bypassing PromptShield or leaking provider secrets.

## Effort Estimate
6-8 hours.

## Implementation
1. Study the current runtime topology and document exact behavior.
   - `docker-compose.yml`: PromptShield Gateway, PromptShield Engine, dashboard, web, log-fwd, Postgres, Bifrost service definitions.
   - `nginx/nginx.conf`: public `/v1/`, `/health`, dashboard, internal/admin, and `/bifrost/` routing.
   - `README.md` and `.env.example`: production setup and operator instructions.
   - `promptshield-src/packages/api/src/routers/gateway.ts`: current PromptShield provider/key config API that may conflict with Bifrost ownership.
   - `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.config.tsx` and `_layout.tsx`: current dashboard navigation and config UX.

2. Create a concrete topology contract for implementation.
   - Add or update documentation in `README.md` describing the accepted production request path: client -> Nginx `/v1/*` -> PromptShield Gateway -> Bifrost `/v1` -> provider.
   - Document that Bifrost is the provider/router control plane and PromptShield is the inline security layer.
   - Document whether `/bifrost/` is local/admin-only and must not be used as the public inference endpoint.
   - Document the expected health checks for PromptShield Gateway, PromptShield Engine, dashboard, and Bifrost.

3. Sanitize and harden production configuration guidance.
   - Update `.env.example` to separate PromptShield security env vars from Bifrost router env vars.
   - Ensure examples do not imply provider keys belong in PromptShield when Bifrost is the router.
   - Call out that real provider keys must not be committed.
   - Identify tracked `bifrost-data` files that contain secrets or mutable runtime state and decide whether to remove from git in a follow-up task.

4. Add lightweight automated verification for static topology risks.
   - Prefer a small script or test under a repo-appropriate location such as `scripts/verify-production-topology.sh` or another existing test location if one is discovered.
   - Verify `nginx/nginx.conf` routes `/v1/` to PromptShield, not Bifrost.
   - Verify `docker-compose.yml` sets PromptShield's OpenAI-compatible upstream to Bifrost's `/v1` endpoint.
   - Verify production docs/env do not present Bifrost `/v1` as the public inference URL.
   - Verification must fail with clear messages when the topology is accidentally weakened.

5. Run verification.
   - Run the new topology verification command.
   - Run any existing lightweight repo checks that are practical after inspecting package scripts, such as `bun run check-types` inside `promptshield-src` if dependencies are available and the change touches TypeScript.
   - Record any unavailable checks and why they could not run.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] `README.md` states the one-product topology and names PromptShield as mandatory pre-routing enforcement.
- [ ] `.env.example` no longer encourages PromptShield-owned provider keys for the unified product; Bifrost is identified as provider/router owner.
- [ ] Static verification exists and fails if `/v1/` is routed directly to Bifrost or if PromptShield no longer forwards to Bifrost.
- [ ] Static verification checks for public-doc/config language that would encourage Bifrost inference bypass.
- [ ] Any tracked Bifrost runtime data containing secrets is identified explicitly for the next task or removed if clearly safe in this task.
- [ ] Verification commands have been run and their results recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README and env examples clearly describe a single secure gateway product.
- Static topology verification passes in the current repo and would fail on direct public Bifrost inference routing.
- No real provider secrets are added; existing secret-bearing runtime state is explicitly addressed.
- The task stays within topology/docs/static verification scope.

## Anti-Patterns
- FORBIDDEN: Do not expose Bifrost `/v1/*` publicly as the documented production endpoint.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not add a custom proxy/router implementation.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not move provider routing back into PromptShield config.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not commit real provider keys, tokens, database dumps with secrets, or mutable runtime state as product defaults.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not make broad UI refactors in this task; UI consolidation should be a later task informed by this topology contract.

## Files To Inspect Or Touch
- `README.md`
- `.env.example`
- `docker-compose.yml`
- `nginx/nginx.conf`
- `promptshield-src/packages/api/src/routers/gateway.ts` (inspect only unless a narrow wording/config change is required)
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.config.tsx` (inspect only)
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.tsx` (inspect only)
- New verification script or test file, location to choose based on existing repo conventions.
acceptance_criteria:
- README and env examples clearly describe a single secure gateway product.
- Static topology verification passes in the current repo and would fail on direct public Bifrost inference routing.
- No real provider secrets are added; existing secret-bearing runtime state is explicitly addressed without printing secret values.
- The task stays within topology/docs/static verification scope.
- Dependency checks (`br dep tree aegis-k9t` and `br dep cycles`) are clean before closing.
notes:
## SRE Refinement Review
Overall assessment: APPROVE with additions below. The task is bounded to 6-8 hours, has a concrete deliverable, and avoids broad UI implementation. The additions below must be honored during execution.

## 1. Granularity
- Estimated 6-8 hours, acceptable for one feature task.
- Deliverable is independently completable: docs/config/static verification for the production topology.
- Do not expand into dashboard UI consolidation; create the next task after this one closes.

## 2. Implementability
- Executor must choose the smallest existing-convention location for the verification command.
- If no `scripts/` directory exists, create `scripts/verify-production-topology.sh` at repo root.
- The script must use deterministic static checks only; do not require Docker services or provider API keys.
- If parsing YAML is needed and no parser is available, prefer targeted shell checks with clear failure messages over adding a new dependency.

## 3. Success Criteria Quality
- Each success criterion must be demonstrated by file diff plus command output.
- The topology verification must produce a non-zero exit if any required invariant fails.
- The final implementation note must list every verification command run and its result.

## 4. Dependencies
- Parent-child dependency is correct: `aegis-k9t.1` is a child of epic `aegis-k9t`.
- This task intentionally has no blocking sibling dependencies because it is the first task.
- Before closing, run `br dep tree aegis-k9t` and `br dep cycles` to confirm structure remains clean.

## 5. Safety Standards
- Do not print, copy, or preserve real provider API keys in docs or scripts.
- If `bifrost-data/config.json` or SQLite DBs contain secrets, prefer documenting removal/sanitization as the next task unless removing them is clearly safe and does not break expected local state.
- Do not make Nginx route changes that accidentally expose Bifrost inference directly.
- Do not alter PromptShield policy behavior beyond docs/static verification in this task.

## 6. Edge Cases and Failure Modes
- Nginx route ambiguity: `/v1/` must not match a Bifrost upstream by rewrite or proxy_pass; verification should check both upstream names and route blocks.
- Public bypass language: README and `.env.example` must not tell production users to call `:8081/v1` or `/bifrost/v1` for inference.
- Local admin exception: If `/bifrost/` remains documented, label it admin/local UI access, not public inference.
- Compose default drift: Verification should catch changes from `http://bifrost:8081/v1` to any non-Bifrost upstream and changes that remove PromptShield's `openai-compatible` mode.
- Secret handling: Detection must not echo full secret values. If scanning tracked files, report file paths and key names, not secret values.
- Port confusion: Docs must distinguish public Nginx ports from internal service ports.

## 7. Red Flag Check
No placeholders are allowed in the final task output. Avoid vague phrases like "harden config" unless accompanied by exact file/setting changes. No TODO stubs in scripts or docs.

## 8. Test Meaningfulness
Required static verification scenarios:
- `test_public_v1_routes_to_promptshield_not_bifrost`: catches accidental direct Bifrost exposure.
- `test_promptshield_upstream_points_to_bifrost_v1`: catches broken PromptShield-to-Bifrost chaining.
- `test_docs_do_not_document_public_bifrost_inference`: catches bypass instructions in README/env examples.
- `test_secret_bearing_bifrost_runtime_state_is_flagged`: catches committed runtime/provider key state without printing secrets.

These tests/checks must assert specific topology invariants, not merely that files exist.

title: Task 2: Consolidate dashboard around Bifrost router control plane
description:
## Goal
Make the dashboard/admin surface reflect the unified product architecture: PromptShield is the inline security layer, Bifrost is the provider/router control plane, and operators should not see PromptShield provider/key routing as the primary gateway configuration path.

## Effort Estimate
6-8 hours.

## Implementation
1. Study current dashboard navigation and routes.
   - `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.tsx`: sidebar sections and labels.
   - `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.config.tsx`: Gateway and Detection Engine config tabs.
   - `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.gateway.tsx`: older PromptShield provider/key/model route editor that may conflict with Bifrost ownership.
   - `promptshield-src/packages/api/src/routers/gateway.ts`: dashboard API shape for PromptShield gateway health/config.
   - `promptshield-src/packages/env/src/server.ts`: current env vars available to dashboard server.
   - `README.md` and `.env.example`: terminology introduced by `aegis-k9t.1`.

2. Add a minimal Bifrost-aware product status/control surface.
   - Add server env support for `BIFROST_URL` with default `http://bifrost:8081` in production Compose and local-friendly fallback as appropriate.
   - Add protected API query for Bifrost health/status using `BIFROST_URL`, with timeout and safe error handling.
   - Update the dashboard overview/status area to show PromptShield Gateway, PromptShield Engine, and Bifrost/Router status as one product.
   - Add an admin-router entry or link for Bifrost provider/router management that clearly points to `/bifrost/` as admin UI only.

3. Reframe or hide conflicting PromptShield provider routing UX.
   - Ensure the main sidebar/config navigation does not direct operators to PromptShield-owned provider/key/model routing as the combined product's provider control plane.
   - If `_layout.gateway.tsx` remains compiled and route-accessible, add a clear guard/banner or redirect-style treatment explaining provider routing is managed in Bifrost for this deployment.
   - Do not remove PromptShield health, policy, audit, or engine controls.

4. Add tests or static checks that catch regression.
   - Extend `scripts/verify-production-topology.sh` or add a focused dashboard/product check that verifies:
     - `BIFROST_URL` is documented/configured.
     - Dashboard code exposes/checks Bifrost router status.
     - Main navigation includes router/admin wording or Bifrost link.
     - Main navigation does not expose the legacy PromptShield provider-routing page as the primary provider control plane.
   - Prefer deterministic static checks unless there is an existing test harness for the web/API layer.

5. Run verification.
   - Run `bash scripts/verify-production-topology.sh`.
   - Run any new dashboard/product static check.
   - Run TypeScript checks for touched PromptShield packages if practical: `cd promptshield-src && bun run check-types`.
   - Run `br dep tree aegis-k9t` and `br dep cycles` before closing.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Dashboard overview/status presents PromptShield Gateway, PromptShield Engine, and Bifrost router status together.
- [ ] Operators have a clear Bifrost admin/router entry point for provider/key/routing management.
- [ ] Main product navigation does not present legacy PromptShield provider/key routing as the provider control plane.
- [ ] `BIFROST_URL` is supported in server env and Compose/env examples.
- [ ] Static or automated checks fail if Bifrost router status/link disappears or the legacy PromptShield provider control plane is reintroduced as primary navigation.
- [ ] Relevant type/static checks pass.

## Anti-Patterns
- FORBIDDEN: Do not implement provider/key storage in PromptShield dashboard for the unified product.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not expose Bifrost `/v1/*` as the public inference endpoint.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not remove PromptShield policy, audit, engine health, or gateway health controls.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not create a full Bifrost dashboard clone in this task; a minimal status plus admin entry point is enough.
- FORBIDDEN: Do not print or commit provider secrets.

## Files Likely To Touch
- `promptshield-src/packages/env/src/server.ts`
- `promptshield-src/packages/api/src/routers/dashboard.ts` or `gateway.ts`
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.dashboard.tsx`
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.tsx`
- `promptshield-src/apps/web/src/routes/_layout.gateway.tsx` if guarding/reframing the old route is needed
- `docker-compose.yml`
- `.env.example`
- `scripts/verify-production-topology.sh` or a new verification script
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard/API exposes Bifrost router status alongside PromptShield Gateway and Engine status.
- Main navigation or dashboard provides clear Bifrost router/admin access without presenting Bifrost as public inference.
- Legacy PromptShield provider/key/model routing is not presented as the primary provider control plane.
- `BIFROST_URL` is supported in server env, Compose, and `.env.example`.
- Static verification and relevant TypeScript checks pass.
notes:
## SRE Refinement Review
Overall assessment: APPROVE with required guardrails. This task is acceptable at 6-8 hours if it stays focused on minimal Bifrost status/admin entry and legacy PromptShield routing de-emphasis.

## 1. Granularity
- Keep scope to one API status query, one dashboard/navigation update, and deterministic checks.
- Do not build provider CRUD, key management, routing rule editors, or a Bifrost dashboard clone.

## 2. Implementability
- Use existing patterns in `dashboardRouter`, `gatewayRouter`, `StatusPill`, and sidebar `NavLink` components.
- Prefer adding `BIFROST_URL` to server env and dashboard service env rather than overloading `GATEWAY_URL`.
- The Bifrost status query should return `{ online, latencyMs, url }` and degrade safely to offline on timeout/network errors.
- External/admin link should target `/bifrost/` and be labeled as router/admin access, not inference.

## 3. Success Criteria Quality
- Verify with code-level checks plus `bun run check-types` if TypeScript files change.
- The static check must fail if `BIFROST_URL` support is removed, if Bifrost status is not queried, or if main nav exposes `/gateway` as provider routing.

## 4. Dependencies
- Parent-child dependency to `aegis-k9t` is correct.
- This task follows `aegis-k9t.1`; do not close the epic after this task unless all epic criteria are objectively met.

## 5. Safety Standards
- Do not add provider API key fields or storage to PromptShield dashboard.
- Do not log URLs containing credentials; `BIFROST_URL` must be base URL only.
- Do not expose Bifrost inference paths in dashboard copy.
- Do not remove existing PromptShield policy/audit/engine functionality.

## 6. Edge Cases and Failure Modes
- Bifrost offline: dashboard must render offline status without throwing.
- Misconfigured `BIFROST_URL`: env validation should reject invalid URLs at startup, consistent with existing env patterns.
- Admin link behind reverse proxy: use `/bifrost/` for browser navigation instead of Docker-internal `http://bifrost:8081`.
- Route confusion: if legacy `/gateway` page remains reachable, it must not look like the primary provider control plane.
- SSR/browser split: do not reference server-only env directly in client code except through tRPC/query data.
- TypeScript strictness: avoid implicit `any`, broken query option names, or missing route imports.

## 7. Red Flag Check
Reject broad rewrites, marketing copy, new provider secret forms, TODO placeholders, or disabling TypeScript errors.

## 8. Test Meaningfulness
Required checks/scenarios:
- `test_dashboard_has_bifrost_router_status`: catches loss of Bifrost status query/display.
- `test_bifrost_url_is_configured`: catches missing env/Compose/example support.
- `test_router_admin_link_is_not_public_inference`: catches links/copy that point users at Bifrost `/v1`.
- `test_legacy_promptshield_provider_route_not_primary_nav`: catches reintroduction of PromptShield provider routing as main provider control plane.

title: Remediation: Block Bifrost admin proxy inference bypass
description:
## Goal
Close the Bifrost admin proxy bypass found by task review: `/bifrost/v1/*` must not proxy to Bifrost inference routes and bypass PromptShield.

## Effort Estimate
2-4 hours.

## Implementation
1. Update `nginx/nginx.conf` so `/bifrost/v1/` cannot reach Bifrost.
   - Add a higher-priority location before the existing `/bifrost/` proxy, such as `location ^~ /bifrost/v1/ { return 404; }` or an equivalent explicit block.
   - Ensure `/bifrost/` remains available for admin UI access.
   - Do not block the public `/v1/` PromptShield route.

2. Extend static verification in `scripts/verify-production-topology.sh`.
   - Add a check that confirms `/bifrost/v1/` is explicitly blocked before the `/bifrost/` proxy.
   - Add a regression check that fails if `/bifrost/` rewrites/proxies all subpaths without an inference-path block.
